Per Justice Gajendra Singh:
This criminal appeal under section 374(2) of the Cr.P.C is preferred challenging the conviction under section 302 & 201 of the IPC and sentence of life imprisonment and 7 years RI to be run concurrently and fine of Rs.5,000/- and Rs.1,000/- with default stipulation and six months and three months RI vide judgment dated 29.12.2017 in Sessions Trial No.376/15 by Addl. Sessions Judge, Manavar, district Dhar for committing murder of Santosh s/o Ramesh on 19.08.2015 at NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3361 2 CRA-1138-2018 10.27 and causing disappearance of evidence of that offence.

sentences.text: Marg No.56 of 2015 was registered and enquiry was conducted.
After enquiry an offence under sections 302, 201 of the IPC was registered against unknown persons on 19.08.2015 at police station Gandhwani, district Dhar.

Matter was investigated and the complicity of the appellant/accused was discovered with the facts that on 17.08.2015 deceased Santosh s/o Ramesh and witness Karan were consuming liquor at the house of appellant/accused and the wife of appellant/accused was serving liquor to deceased Santosh with compromising gestures.
Due to this, appellant/accused got provoked and assaulted deceased Santosh and Karan.
Santosh was assaulted with sickle on the head and assaulted Karan with a stick.

Santosh succumbed to the injuries and to cause disappearance of the evidence of this offence he thrown the body of Santosh in a well belonging to Nathu and a report was submitted to the Court of JMFC where criminal case no.1115/2015 was registered and vide order dated 13.11.2015 the case was committed to the Court of Sessions.
3. Appellant/accused abjured guilt and to bring home the guilt, prosecution examined eye witness Karan as PW/5 and wife of appellant/accuwed Surajbai as PW/8 and witness Sonu Sen as PW/1,

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3361 3 CRA-1138-2018 Nathu as PW/2, Medical Officer Dr.Sandeep Shrivastav as PW/3, Kanha as PW/4, Ramesh as PW/6, sub Inspector Kailash as PW/7 and Inspector Mukesh as PW/9.

In cross examination under section 313 of the Cr.P.C,
appellant/accused either expressed ignorance or stated the circumstances appearing against him as false.
His probable defence through cross examination of the prosecution witnesses is that Karan (PW/5) caused the murder of Santosh and falsely implicated the appellant/accused.
No evidence was adduced in defence.

4. Appreciating the prosecution evidence, trial court found the testimony of Karan (PW/5) as reliable and also relied the fact that a sickle, stick of teak wood, a shirt recovered on the memorandum Ex.P/10 were forwarded to FSL, Sagar and report Ex.P/17 of FSL, Indore reported that shirt, sickle and stick of teak wood have blood and there is no explanation of the appellant/accused in this regard and concluded that the act of the appellant/accused falls within clause 3rd of section 300 of the IPC and convicted the appellant/accused under section 302 of the IPC for committing murder of Santosh and causing disappearance of the body of the deceased and passed sentence as mentioned in para-1 of the judgment.
5. This appeal has been preferred on the ground that Karan (PW/5) was silent for a period of six days and no plausible explanation has been adduced by the prosecution.
The FSL report Ex.P/17 does not help the prosecution.

The deceased Santosh was seen with Karan on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3361 4 CRA-1138-2018 17.08.2015 last time and father and father and brother of the deceased have suspected Karan regarding disappearance of Santosh and trial court has ignored these vital circumstances.

6. Heard.
7.
Government Advocate has supported the conviction and sentence and submitted that the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: Perused the record.
9. On re-appreciation of the testimony of Karan (PW/5) who was present at the time of incident at the house of appellant/accused, his testimony is reliable.
It does not create doubt regarding presence of the witness at the time of incident at the house of appellant/accused and trial court did not commit any error in relying the testimony of Karan (PW/5).
The trial court has recorded reasons regarding hostility of Surajbai (PW/8) as her husband is the accused in this case and the reasons recorded by the trial court are proper in this regard.
Recovery of sickle, teak wood and blood stained shirt on 1st of September, 2015 vide Ex.P/11 on the information Ex.P/10 is duly proved from the testimony of Kailash (PW/7).
There is no explanation on behalf of the appellant/accused regarding the FSL report, Indore (Ex.P/17) that found blood stains on the sickle, teak wood and shirt recovered from the appellant/accused.

Accordingly, the finding of the trial court that appellant/accused is the person who caused death of Santosh by assaulting him with sickle on the head resulting in fracture is based on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3361 5 CRA-1138-2018 proper appreciation of occular testimony, circumstantial evidence as well as medical evidence.
Now the question arises whether trial court has rightly convicted the appellant/accused under section 302 of the IPC or his act falls under section 304 of the IPC.

10. Trial court has recorded the finding that act of the appellant/accused falls within clause-3 of section 300 of the IPC and also recorded the finding in para-38 that at the time of incident wife of appellant/accused was serving liquor to deceased Santosh and accused has objected and this was the motive of commission of offence.

Trial court has also recorded the finding in para-17 that at that time Surajbai (PW/8) was indulged in a very familiar and intimate chatting with deceased Santosh in the absence of appellant/accused and Surajbai (PW/8) also served liquor to deceased Santosh and appellant/accused returned to home at 8.00 p.m and rebuked Surajbai for chatting with the deceased Santosh and serving him liquor and got provoked and assaulted with sickle on the back side of head.
This circumstances had not been taken into consideration by the trial court.

11. In Saroj @ Suraj Panchal vs. State of West Bengal - (2014) 4 SCC 802 Apex Court has considered the fact situation in which family members viz. father and brother of the girl have seen the deceased with the daughter and beat the deceased with iron rod and lathi and dragged him by tying his hands and legs through the wooden staircase from the first floor to the ground floor and left him in the danga of Govinda NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3361 6 CRA-1138-2018 Mondal and the deceased succumbed to the injuries.

entities.text: Saroj @ Suraj Panchal vs. State of West Bengal - (2014) 4 SCC 802
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In these circumstances, the Apex Court concluded that the death was caused by the act of appellant/accused done with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death and, therefore, the offence would squarely come within the first part of section 304 of the IPC and set aside the conviction of the appellants/accused under section 302 r/w section 34 of the IPC.
The facts situation bears great similarity to that in the decision in Mangesh vs. State of Maharashtra - (2011) 2 SCC 123 and State of Punjab vs. Jagtar Singh & others (2011) 14 SCC 678 .

Appellant/accused entered his house suddenly and he provoked on seeing that his wife is serving liquor to the deceased and is chatting with him in cheerful gestures and the Mukut @ Mugut vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173115556/

sentences.text: accused/appellant picked the instrument of offence from the house and the instrument of offence viz. sickle which is used generally as an agricultural equipment.
Accordingly, this case also falls within part-I of section 304 of the IPC and not under section 302 of the IPC.
Accordingly, the conviction of the appellant/accused under section 302 of the IPC is set aside and he is convicted under section 304 Part-I and 201 of the IPC.

13. Appellant/accused has undergone the sentence as per certificate dated 22.08.2023 of Warrant Officer, Central Jail, Badwani which is reproduced as below:
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3361 7 CRA-1138-2018 .

This certificate was issued one year 5 months and 27 days ago and during this period also the appellant/accused was under custody and the total jail sentence is sufficient for the offence under section 304 Part-I and 201 of the IPC which are ordered to be run concurrently.
Hence, the sentence of the appellant/accused is reduced to the period already undergone.
Supersession warrant be prepared.
The appellant be set at liberty forthwith, if not required in any other criminal case.
Accordingly, this appeal is partly allowed to that extent.
